title: Apply-time answer families bind the five elicits to the wizard contract
description: When the applying project answers the five apply-time elicits, the wizard honours each with a runtime clause per family: `blueprint.json.elicits[id=step-manifest]` populates the step order the task-list enumerates; `blueprint.json.elicits[id=navigation]` picks the linear-vs-free branch on TAC-2501 (linear gates rows by prerequisites; free allows anchor navigation to every row); `blueprint.json.elicits[id=step-indicator]` picks the indicator surface owned by `ADR-2503.decision`; `blueprint.json.elicits[id=draft-transport]` picks the draft-store backend on TAC-2503 (spa-local-storage default; server-scoped delegates to the applied persistence blueprint; none disables draft persistence); `blueprint.json.elicits[id=validation-policy]` sets the on-blur/on-change/on-submit gate on TAC-2502.
rationale: The five apply-time answer families named in the guide needed one must REQ per family so a project cannot elicit a value and see it ignored silently.
